claims.value: Recovered prior state: PVE34 remains historical proof of the split fetch/DB architecture and DB/write bottleneck, including the validated 10.019M run and roughly 403–408 PGCR/sec final crossing performance. source_paths: Projects/Warmind/D1 parser autonomy and autotuning context summary - 2026-05-25.md

claims.value: The new explicit operator constraint replaces the open-ended longer-alpha action with one 30-minute dev-only soak. It cannot change production or add durable controller persistence; batch 128 is the initial ceiling while fetch may adapt. Acceptance requires at least 900 PGCR/sec steady during the final 10 minutes, zero integrity or recovery violations, no DB connection failure storm, and successful restart from DB truth after the controlled stop. Abort and roll back if MySQL exceeds 90% of host memory for two consecutive minutes or DB connection failures exceed three per minute.

The bounded-alpha constraint is new operator authority, not historical performance evidence, and it does not supersede existing integrity and recovery rules. DB rows remain truth; raw-marker commits travel with summaries; failed rows retry immediately; DB/cache availability failure stops rather than spins; restart scans and fills gaps. The trial has no production mutation, rebuild/recompute path, parser-state correctness table, Cortex S3 replay into DB writes, or durable controller persistence.

answer.answer: Revised child checkpoint committed as checkpoint:f7585449-1945-d53e-0e0e-72ed29a48640. The buildable plan uses three separate level-0 cores, with one requested heavy machine per core and construction gated by complete per-core heat ledgers.

claims.value: The recovered architecture replaces the superseded mega-base with a modular backbone-and-spurs network of protected production cells and mining spurs. Update 1 rails carry power and items, with v.1/v.2/v.3 throughput of 120/240/480 items per minute.

The revised requirement is one 500-heat Constructorizer plus two 650-heat Facturers, totaling 1,800 heat. Each level-0 Base Core provides only 1,000 capacity, and exceeding it disables Fire Wave protection.

Use three separate level-0 cores: Core A gets only the Constructorizer, leaving at most 500 heat for existing and supporting load; Cores B and C each get one Facturer, leaving at most 350 apiece. Reject Constructorizer-plus-Facturer at 1,150, two Facturers at 1,300, and all three at 1,800 because every combination exceeds one core's 1,000 capacity.

Before construction, verify the live Update 1 build menu and record each candidate core's current load. Add all required support heat to the 500/650/650 machine loads and build one cell at a time only when its projected total is at most 1,000 and Fire Wave protection remains active. Exclude hidden, future, and pre-Update-1 equipment—including Rail v.4/v.5—and do not rely on disputed amplifier capacity without in-game verification.

checkpoint.objective: Build and operate an Update 1-only distributed factory with one Constructorizer and two Facturers while every Base Core remains level 0 and every occupied core retains Fire Wave protection.

decisions: Core A hosts only the Constructorizer; Cores B and C each host only one Facturer.
Complete per-core load, including existing and supporting buildings, must remain at or below 1,000.
Unsafe heavy-machine co-location is rejected.
Only live Update 1 equipment is authoritative; hidden, future, and pre-Update-1 content remains excluded.
open_questions: What load already exists under each candidate core?
Are all required machines, recipes, inputs, power sources, buffers, and rail components unlocked?

next_actions: Capture the live build menu and three candidate Core panels.
Prepare complete per-core heat ledgers before placing any machine.
Commission one cell at a time and recheck load and Fire Wave protection after every placement.
Connect cells using unlocked Update 1 rails and upgrade trunks only when measured throughput requires it.

answer.answer: Advanced Straylight from evaluation into implementation and committed child checkpoint checkpoint:9d19d3e1-a12f-a504-607b-66589b2b3b3b at corpus generation 3993.

claims.value: Straylight is an agent-first portable context and durable-work layer that preserves learned knowledge, evidence, provenance, and live resumable work state; retrieval-only performance is a regression lane rather than the product-success gate.

Cumulative cached replay and uncached input are separate accounting categories: cached replay must not be interpreted as reducing uncached prompt input. Report both separately. The frozen one-shot BM25 baseline passed 17/20 cases, recovered 48/53 evidence items, and used about 1,070 mean estimated tokens; its shell implementation is only a regression fixture.

The first persistent build slice is an end-to-end revision transition: reopen a named parent checkpoint pinned at revision N, refresh to N+1 with an evidence/constraint diff, provide batched typed query/read using exact and lexical retrieval behind a pluggable semantic interface, and atomically commit an immutable child naming its parent and retaining exact source references.

The transition gate passes only when each case uses at most four completed workspace calls, matches every required direct-filesystem answer claim, exposes the N-to-N+1 diff, exercises exact plus lexical retrieval with a callable semantic-provider seam, creates one immutable parent-linked child retaining cited sources, avoids full-corpus reconstruction when checkpoint plus delta suffice, and reports cumulative cached replay separately from uncached input.

checkpoint.objective: Implement and gate the first persistent, snapshot-pinned Straylight workspace transition slice.
current_state: The project-owner transition decision advances Straylight from evaluation into implementation.
Token accounting now distinguishes cumulative cached replay from uncached input.
The one-shot BM25 regression baseline is 17/20 cases, 48/53 evidence items, and about 1,070 mean estimated tokens.
Child checkpoint checkpoint:9d19d3e1-a12f-a504-607b-66589b2b3b3b was committed at generation 3993.
decisions: Implement the parent-resume, revision-refresh/diff, typed batched retrieval/read, and immutable child-checkpoint path first.
Use exact and lexical retrieval behind a pluggable semantic interface.
Reuse bounded checkpoint and delta evidence instead of reconstructing the corpus when sufficient.
Keep broader storage, deployment, schema, and semantic-backend selection outside the first slice.
open_questions: Which semantic backend should be selected after the transition contract passes?
What absolute cached-replay and uncached-input budgets should be established after separate harness measurement?
next_actions: Implement persistent workspace/session storage and the typed transition contracts.
Add an end-to-end N-to-N+1 fixture with direct-filesystem oracle assertions.
Run the measurable transition gate and preserve BM25 as a regression comparison.
